newsitem.title: USA: Harrah's Entertainment rights plan upheld.
newsitem.headline: Harrah's Entertainment rights plan upheld.

text.p: Harrah's Entertainment Inc shareholders have apparently rejected a proposal to eliminate a shareholder rights plan, the company said Friday.
Harrah's said preliminary voting results from the inspector of election showed 32.7 percent voting for the proposal, well short of the 75 percent needed to pass it.

"The company had earlier announced expected failure of the measure based on the votes received and counted as of the annual meeting on April 25," it said. "Today's vote tally, though not yet finalized, represents all votes received."
Harrah's said it will include the final voting results in its 10-Q filing on May 15.

Last Friday, the company said preliminary voting results showed the proposal, to amend its by-laws to redeem the rights plan and require approval by a majority vote for adoption of any such plan in the future, failed to pass.
The proposal was sponsored by Hotel Employees and Restaurant Employees International Union, which called the 75-percent requirement illegal.
Harrah's has defended the requirement, saying it was upheld by state law.
